mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding future equity value.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of FEDFUNDS > 4.0 regimes, or IC > 0.05 over 5-year horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, wage growth accelerates and consumer confidence rises, both of which are associated with stronger S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: IC < 0.03 over 10-year window when trigger is met, or 20-day returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) relative to GDP signals excess demand, which predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates sustained earnings growth.
failure_condition: Rank IC > 0.10 over 60-day horizon or 60-day returns underperform 20-day moving average by >2%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls by more than 2% in two consecutive months, it indicates supply-side weakness that is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates soft earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day IC > 0.15 when trigger occurs, or 5-day returns are not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three months suggests disinflation, which typically precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as rate-cut expectations rise.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of CPIAUCSL declines of >1% over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% for the first time in a 6-month window, it often coincides with a regime shift to labor market tightening that is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates wage suppression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 and UNRATE was >= 4.0 for the previous 6 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in >60% of such transitions, or IC < 0.05 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising homebuilding (HOUST) above 1,000K units indicate a rebound in consumer confidence and construction spending, which predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns underperform baseline by >5% when HOUST > 1,000K for 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to GDP (INDPRO/GDP) falls below 0.95 for three consecutive months, it suggests supply-side constraints that are associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates earnings compression.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative or IC > 0.10 when trigger is met.
